question: What is the primary purpose of evaluation in nursing practice?

options.A: To replace the need for physical patient assessments
options.B: To determine the effectiveness of nursing interventions
options.C: To punish staff who make clinical errors
options.D: To increase the paperwork load for head nurses

explanation: Evaluation measures whether the care provided actually met the patient's health goals and needs. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h1)

question: Why is structured evaluation essential for nursing schools in Nigeria?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any written examinations
options.B: It guarantees adherence to professional standards and quality education
options.C: It ensures students never fail any clinical procedure
options.D: It reduces the duration of clinical postings for students

explanation: Regular evaluation ensures that training programs consistently meet the required competencies for safe practice. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h1)

question: What core principle ensures an evaluation tool measures what it is supposed to measure?
explanation: Validity directly addresses whether an assessment tool accurately captures the specific concept or skill it was designed for. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h2)

question: A clinical instructor uses a checklist that gives the exact same score for a student's wound dressing technique when used on different days by different supervisors. Which principle is best demonstrated?
explanation: Consistency across different evaluators and time points points directly to a reliable assessment tool. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h2)

question: What type of evaluation is conducted at the end of a training program to judge overall success?
explanation: Summative evaluations happen at the conclusion of a course or intervention to measure final outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h3)

question: A nurse checks a patient's baseline vital signs before starting a new medication regimen. What type of evaluation does this represent?
explanation: Baseline assessments done before an intervention begins serve a diagnostic purpose by identifying starting points and potential risks. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h3)

question: What assessment method uses a series of stations to test various practical clinical skills?
explanation: An OSCE rotates students through practical stations to evaluate hands-on clinical competence systematically. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h4)

question: A nursing lecturer wants to evaluate a student's ability to perform sterile wound dressing without missing steps. Which tool is most appropriate?
explanation: Observational checklists let the evaluator check off each specific procedural step as the student performs it live. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h4)

question: Why can an evaluation tool fail to be valid even if it consistently gives the same scores?

options.A: It takes too long to administer to students
options.B: It may consistently measure the wrong skill set
options.C: It is written in a language students understand
options.D: It requires too many supervisors in the room

explanation: Reliability means consistency, but if the test measures irrelevant traits, it lacks validity despite being reliable. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h5)

question: What is a common threat to the reliability of a clinical grading process?

options.A: Using questions that match actual clinical practice
options.B: Inconsistent scoring standards among different evaluators
options.C: Providing clear rubrics to all participating students
options.D: Allowing adequate time for the practical examination

explanation: When different examiners grade using their own subjective feelings rather than a rubric, reliability drops significantly. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h5)

question: What term describes giving a student an inflated grade because the evaluator simply likes their personality?
explanation: The halo effect occurs when a positive general impression of someone clouds specific, objective judgment of their performance. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h6)

question: Why do nurses sometimes falsify clinical incident reports or skip thorough evaluations in busy wards?

options.A: Strict adherence to hospital management policy
options.B: Abundant time and staff availability on duty
options.C: A desire to improve patient safety outcomes

explanation: Punitive environments discourage honest reporting and evaluation, forcing staff to hide mistakes out of self-preservation. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h6)

question: A patient's care plan for a pressure ulcer shows no healing after two weeks of current dressing changes. What is the appropriate next step based on the evaluation phase?

options.A: Mark the care plan as successfully completed
options.B: Reassess the patient and modify the care plan
options.C: Blame the junior nurses for poor documentation
options.D: Discontinue all documentation regarding the wound

explanation: Evaluation requires changing interventions when outcomes show that goals are not being achieved. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h7)

question: How do nurse managers use evaluation principles in a hospital ward?

options.A: To avoid scheduling shifts for junior nursing staff
options.B: To audit ward operations and appraise staff performance
options.C: To replace physicians during ward morning rounds
options.D: To eliminate the need for patient care conferences

explanation: Managers apply evaluation to monitor staff output, quality of care, and overall operational efficiency. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h7)
